questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding poverty line committees in India:
1. The Lakdawala Expert Group estimated state-specific poverty lines, updated using CPI-IW for urban areas and CPI-AL for rural areas.
2. The Tendulkar Committee re-adopted the calorie norms of 2,400 kcal (rural) and 2,100 kcal (urban) as the sole basis of the poverty line.
3. The Alagh Task Force of 1979 based the poverty line on the calorie norms of 2,400 kcal (rural) and 2,100 kcal (urban) per person per day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Alagh set the calorie-based line and Lakdawala made it state-specific using CPI-IW and CPI-AL. Tendulkar moved away from the calorie-only norm and added private spending on health and education to the consumption basket, so statement 2 reverses its approach.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Poverty, Inequality and Unemployment chapter)
questions.h: Alagh sets calories, Lakdawala splits by state, Tendulkar leaves calories.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Expert Group) with List-II (Feature of its poverty estimation):
List-I
A. Alagh Task Force
B. Lakdawala Expert Group
C. Tendulkar Committee
D. Rangarajan Expert Group
List-II
1. State-specific poverty lines updated with CPI-IW and CPI-AL
2. Calorie norms of 2,400 kcal (rural) and 2,100 kcal (urban)
3. Uniform poverty line basket for rural and urban areas, including private spending on health and education
4. Separate rural and urban baskets set at about Rs 972 and Rs 1,407 per person per month for 2011-12
questions.e: Alagh gave the calorie norms, Lakdawala made the lines state-specific, Tendulkar used a uniform basket with health and education spending, and Rangarajan went back to separate baskets with a higher line.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Poverty, Inequality and Unemployment chapter)

questions.q: For the year 2011-12, the Rangarajan Expert Group estimated India's poverty ratio at about
questions.e: The Rangarajan group set higher lines than Tendulkar and so found 29.5 percent poor in 2011-12. The 21.9 percent figure is the Tendulkar estimate for the same year, which is the usual trap.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Poverty, Inequality and Unemployment chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about measures of poverty:
1. The head count ratio shows the proportion of people below the poverty line but not how far below the line they are.
2. The poverty gap index measures the average shortfall of the poor from the poverty line.
3. The Sen index ignores inequality among the poor.
4. The head count ratio is sensitive to the depth of poverty.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Sen index combines the head count ratio, the poverty gap and inequality among the poor, and the head count ratio is blind to depth: a poor person getting poorer does not change it.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Poverty, Inequality and Unemployment chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The head count ratio is considered an incomplete measure of poverty.
Statement-II: It does not capture how far below the poverty line the poor are, nor how income is distributed among them.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The head count ratio only counts the poor. Because it is silent on depth and distribution, measures such as the poverty gap and the Sen index were devised to complement it.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Poverty, Inequality and Unemployment chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):
1. It is published by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative.
2. It uses ten indicators grouped under health, education and standard of living.
3. A person is MPI poor if deprived in at least half of the weighted indicators.
4. The three dimensions are given equal weight.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The cut-off is deprivation in at least one-third of the weighted indicators, not half.
questions.s: UNDP and OPHI, Global MPI methodology; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: In the Global MPI, each of the six indicators under the standard of living dimension carries a weight of
questions.e: Each of the three dimensions has a weight of 1/3. Health and education have two indicators each (1/6 per indicator), while living standards has six indicators sharing the same 1/3, so 1/18 each.
questions.s: UNDP and OPHI, Global MPI methodology

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Multidimensional Poverty Index prepared by NITI Aayog:
1. It uses the Alkire-Foster methodology.
2. It uses 12 indicators, adding maternal health and bank account to the global indicators.
3. Its baseline report used data from the National Family Health Survey 2015-16.
4. Its three dimensions are health, education and standard of living.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The national index adapts the global MPI with two extra indicators (maternal health, bank account), and its baseline in 2021 relied on NFHS-4.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, National MPI baseline report, Nov 2021

questions.q: In the National Multidimensional Poverty Index based on NFHS-5 (2019-21), which State had the highest proportion of population that is multidimensionally poor?
questions.e: Bihar was at the top, followed by Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, while Kerala had the lowest share. The ranking tracks weak sanitation, nutrition and schooling indicators.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, National MPI Progress Review, 2023

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Index (HDI):
1. It aggregates its three dimension indices using the arithmetic mean.
2. Its education component is measured only by the adult literacy rate.
3. Its income component is measured by nominal GDP per capita in US dollars.
4. The first Human Development Report was published in 1990.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 4 is correct. Since 2010 the HDI uses the geometric mean, education is measured by mean and expected years of schooling, and income by GNI per capita in PPP terms.
questions.s: UNDP, Human Development Report; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Statement-I: Since 2010 the HDI has combined its three dimension indices using the geometric mean.
Statement-II: A geometric mean limits substitutability, so poor performance in one dimension is not fully offset by high achievement in another.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The switch from the arithmetic mean was made so that a country cannot cover a weak health or education record with a high income score. That is the reason behind the geometric mean.
questions.s: UNDP, Human Development Report; Ramesh Singh
questions.h: Geometric: weak link drags the whole chain.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Index) with List-II (Components):
List-I
A. Human Development Index
B. Gender Inequality Index
C. Physical Quality of Life Index
D. Global Hunger Index
List-II
1. Life expectancy, years of schooling, gross national income per capita
2. Reproductive health, empowerment, labour market participation
3. Literacy, infant mortality, life expectancy at age one
4. Undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality
questions.e: PQLI, devised by Morris D. Morris, was an early social indicator that excluded income. The HDI later added income, GII measures gender gaps, and GHI uses four hunger-related indicators.
questions.s: UNDP; Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four indicators used to compute the Global Hunger Index?
questions.e: The GHI combines undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality. Literacy is not part of it.
questions.s: Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, GHI methodology

questions.q: The first Human Development Report of 1990, which introduced the Human Development Index, is associated with the work of
o: Joseph Stiglitz, drawing on the Washington Consensus
Mahbub ul Haq, drawing on the capability approach of Amartya Sen
Jeffrey Sachs, drawing on the Millennium Project
W. Arthur Lewis, drawing on the dual-sector model
questions.e: Haq led the UNDP team that built the HDI to shift attention from income to what people can do and be. Sen's capability approach gave it the conceptual base.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Gini coefficient of zero represents perfect equality.
2. The farther the Lorenz curve lies from the line of equality, the greater the inequality.
3. The Palma ratio is the ratio of the income share of the top 10 percent to that of the bottom 10 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Gini is 0 for perfect equality and 1 for perfect inequality, and a bowed-out Lorenz curve means greater inequality. The Palma ratio compares the top 10 percent with the bottom 40 percent.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Inequality; NCERT Class XII Economics

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the demographic dividend:
1. It arises when the share of the working-age population in the total population rises relative to dependents.
2. It is automatic and does not depend on education, skills or employment generation.
3. The dependency ratio is the population aged 0-14 and 65 and above divided by the population aged 15-64, multiplied by 100.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A falling dependency ratio opens a window for higher savings and growth, but the gain has to be earned through health, education and jobs. It is a potential, not an automatic benefit.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Social Sector chapter)
questions.h: Dividend is a window, not a gift.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's demographic dividend could turn into a demographic burden.
Statement-II: A large working-age population that lacks adequate education, skills and productive employment adds to unemployment rather than to growth.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The dividend only pays off when young workers are productively absorbed. Without skills and jobs, the same bulge increases joblessness and social pressure.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Social Sector chapter)

questions.q: As per the National Family Health Survey-5 (2019-21), India's total fertility rate was
questions.e: NFHS-5 recorded a TFR of 2.0 against the replacement level of 2.1. NFHS-4 had 2.2 and NFHS-3 had 2.7, which are the tempting older values.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Family Health Survey (NFHS):
1. The International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai, is the nodal agency for the NFHS rounds.
2. NFHS-5 was conducted during 2019-21.
3. The NFHS is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NFHS is a Ministry of Health and Family Welfare survey with IIPS as the nodal agency. The Registrar General runs the Census and the Sample Registration System, not NFHS.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, which one among the following States had the lowest literacy rate?
questions.e: Bihar's literacy was about 63.8 percent, the lowest among States, against 74.0 percent for India. Kerala was the highest.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, India's child sex ratio in the age group 0-6 years was
questions.e: The child sex ratio fell from 927 in 2001 to 919 in 2011, a sign of sex-selective practices. The figures 933 and 943 are the overall sex ratios of 2001 and 2011.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Population Policy, 2000:
1. Its medium-term objective was to bring the total fertility rate to replacement level by 2010.
2. Its long-term objective was to achieve a stable population by 2045.
3. It made a two-child norm compulsory for all citizens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The policy set targets but kept family planning voluntary and target-free in approach. It did not make a two-child norm compulsory.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MoHFW

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding health in the Constitution of India:
1. 'Public health and sanitation; hospitals and dispensaries' is in the State List.
2. 'Population control and family planning' is in the Union List.
3. Article 47 makes it a duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and improve public health.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Health is largely a State subject, and Article 47 is a Directive Principle. Population control and family planning (Entry 20A) is in the Concurrent List, not the Union List.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY):
1. It covers secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
2. Cover is limited to families with not more than five members.
3. Beneficiary families were identified using the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 deprivation and occupational criteria.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-JAY gives cashless cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation, with entitlement based on SECC data. It was designed with no cap on family size or age.

questions.q: As per the norms for plain areas, a Sub-centre, a Primary Health Centre and a Community Health Centre serve a population of about
questions.e: The plain-area norms are 5,000, 30,000 and 1,20,000. The lower figures of 3,000, 20,000 and 80,000 are for hilly and tribal areas.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MoHFW norms

questions.q:
Arrange the following immunisation initiatives in India in chronological order:
1. Pulse Polio Programme
2. Expanded Programme on Immunisation
3. Mission Indradhanush
4. Universal Immunisation Programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: EPI began in 1978, UIP in 1985, Pulse Polio in 1995 and Mission Indradhanush in December 2014. Each step widened coverage after the previous one.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MoHFW

questions.q: India was certified polio-free by the World Health Organization in
questions.e: India's last wild polio case was in January 2011, and the WHO South-East Asia Region was certified polio-free in March 2014 after three years without a case. In 2012, India was only removed from the list of polio-endemic countries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the POSHAN Abhiyaan:
1. It was launched in 2018 to reduce stunting, undernutrition, anaemia and low birth weight.
2. It uses convergence of nutrition-related schemes and technology such as the ICDS-Common Application Software.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: POSHAN Abhiyaan is the Ministry of Women and Child Development's nutrition mission and works through convergence and technology. It is not run by the health ministry.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a service provided under the Integrated Child Development Services scheme?
questions.e: ICDS (1975) offers six services: supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral. The cash incentive for institutional delivery belongs to the Janani Suraksha Yojana.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MWCD

questions.q: The National Health Policy, 2017 set the goal of raising public health expenditure to what share of GDP by 2025?
questions.e: NHP 2017 set the target at 2.5 percent of GDP by 2025. It was meant to move the system towards assured, preventive and promotive care.

questions.q: The Health Survey and Development Committee of 1946, which recommended integrating preventive and curative services with the primary health unit as the base, was headed by
questions.e: The Bhore Committee laid the blueprint of India's public health system. The Mudaliar Committee (1961) reviewed progress later, and the Kartar Singh Committee (1973) focused on multipurpose workers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Education Policy 2020:
1. The foundational stage covers ages 3 to 8.
2. The preparatory stage covers Grades 3 to 5.
3. The middle stage covers Grades 6 to 10.
4. The secondary stage covers Grades 9 to 10 only.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The middle stage is Grades 6 to 8 and the secondary stage is Grades 9 to 12 in two phases, in the 5+3+3+4 structure.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The National Education Policy 2020 replaces the 10+2 structure with a 5+3+3+4 structure.
Statement-II: The new structure is designed to match the stages of schooling to the cognitive development of children.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The new design brings early childhood education into the formal structure, with each stage tied to the learning needs of that age group. That is the stated reason for the change.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Education Policy 2020:
1. It proposes raising public spending on education to 10 percent of GDP.
2. It targets a Gross Enrolment Ratio of 50 percent in higher education by 2035.
3. It proposes an Academic Bank of Credit to store credits earned by students.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NEP 2020 reiterates public investment of 6 percent of GDP, a goal that dates back to the Kothari Commission, not 10 percent. The GER target and the Academic Bank of Credit are both in the policy.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a recommendation of the National Education Policy 2020?
o: Medium of instruction in the home language or mother tongue at least till Grade 5
Multiple entry and exit options in undergraduate programmes
A single regulator for higher education other than medical and legal education
Compulsory teaching of Hindi as the third language in all States
questions.e: The policy follows a flexible three-language formula and says no language will be imposed on any State. It does recommend home-language instruction, multiple exit points and a single higher education regulator.

questions.q: The draft of the National Education Policy that led to NEP 2020 was prepared by a committee chaired by
questions.e: The committee headed by former ISRO chairman K. Kasturirangan submitted the draft in 2019, and the Union Cabinet approved the policy in July 2020. Kothari headed the 1964-66 Education Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009:
1. Private unaided schools must reserve 10 percent of seats at entry level for disadvantaged children.
2. Every school other than an unaided private school must constitute a School Management Committee.
3. The prescribed pupil-teacher ratio at the primary level is 30:1.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The RTE reservation in private unaided schools is 25 percent at entry level, not 10. School Management Committees and the 30:1 primary ratio are statutory.

questions.q: The RTE (Amendment) Act, 2019 changed the no-detention policy by allowing the appropriate Government to
o: permit detention of children from Class I onwards
permit detention of a child in Class V or Class VIII after a regular examination and re-examination
abolish all examinations up to Class VIII
allow schools to expel children who fail twice
questions.e: The original Act barred any detention till completion of elementary education. The 2019 amendment lets States hold back a child in Class V or VIII if she fails the re-examination.

questions.q: The right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years was made a Fundamental Right by the
questions.e: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A, and also changed Article 45 and added the duty in Article 51A(k). The 93rd Amendment dealt with reservation in private educational institutions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Education was a State subject until the Forty-second Amendment shifted it to the Concurrent List.
2. Education is Entry 25 of the Concurrent List.
3. Coordination and determination of standards in higher education and research is an Entry in the Union List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved education to the Concurrent List. The Union keeps control of standards in higher education through Entry 66 of the Union List.

questions.q:
Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018, integrates which of the following schemes?
1. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
2. Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan
3. Teacher Education
4. Mid-Day Meal Scheme
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Samagra Shiksha treats school education from pre-school to Class 12 as a continuum and merges SSA, RMSA and teacher education. The mid-day meal runs separately as PM POSHAN.

questions.q: The NIPUN Bharat Mission aims to ensure that every child attains foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of
questions.e: NIPUN Bharat, launched in 2021 under Samagra Shiksha, targets universal foundational learning by Grade 3 by 2026-27. This reflects NEP 2020's emphasis on early learning.

questions.q: Which one of the following States is generally credited with pioneering the large-scale mid-day meal scheme in schools?
questions.e: Tamil Nadu began a school meal scheme under K. Kamaraj and later expanded it into a statewide universal programme. The Centre launched a national programme in 1995, now called PM POSHAN.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Survey / Report : Publishing or conducting agency
1. ASER : Pratham
2. UDISE+ : NITI Aayog
3. AISHE : Ministry of Education
4. NFHS : Registrar General and Census Commissioner
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. UDISE+ is run by the Ministry of Education, and NFHS is led by IIPS under the health ministry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan:
1. It provides assured, comprehensive antenatal care free of cost on the 9th of every month.
2. The check-ups are provided by specialist doctors or medical officers.
3. It is a scheme for children under five years under the Mission Indradhanush.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PMSMA, launched in 2016, gives free antenatal check-ups to pregnant women on the 9th of each month to cut maternal and infant deaths. It is a maternal health programme, not part of Mission Indradhanush.

questions.q: The 'Janani Suraksha Yojana' under the National Health Mission is best described as
o: an insurance cover for hospitalisation of the elderly
a free vaccination drive for children below two years
a nutrition scheme for adolescent girls
a conditional cash transfer to promote institutional delivery
questions.e: JSY, started in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission, pays cash to mothers who deliver in health facilities. The aim is to reduce maternal and neonatal deaths.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MoHFW

questions.q: The National Medical Commission Act, 2019 replaced which body as the regulator of medical education?
o: All India Institute of Medical Sciences
questions.e: The NMC took over from the Medical Council of India, whose functioning had been criticised. It also oversees medical ethics and the registration of practitioners.

questions.q: Under the National Health Mission, the Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) is best described as
o: a salaried doctor posted at the Primary Health Centre
an auxiliary nurse midwife at the sub-centre
a community health worker chosen from the village and paid performance-based incentives
a Panchayat official responsible for sanitation
questions.e: ASHAs link the community with the health system, mobilising women for institutional delivery and immunisation. They are paid by incentive rather than a fixed salary.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; MoHFW

questions.q: In the context of health indicators, which one of the following correctly defines the 'stunting' among children under five years?
questions.e: Stunting is low height for age and signals chronic undernutrition, while wasting is low weight for height, a sign of acute undernutrition. Underweight is low weight for age.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Social Sector chapter; NFHS definitions

questions.q: Which one of the following is the main purpose of the Anaemia Mukt Bharat strategy launched in 2018?
o: Providing cashless hospitalisation to poor families
Reducing anaemia among children, adolescents and women through the 6x6x6 strategy
questions.e: Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses six interventions for six beneficiary groups through six institutional mechanisms. It complements POSHAN Abhiyaan.
